questions.question: Burma became independent soverign republic in the year ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Burma became an independent sovereign republic on 4 January **1948**__.
 
• Burma was colonized by Britain in the 19th century.
 
• It got free from the UK on this day.
 
• The country is bordered by India, China, Laos, and Thailand.

questions.question: The river Ganga emerges from Gangotri Glacier and ends at ________.

questions.question: Who presides over the joint sitting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speaker of Lok Sabha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**The __**Speaker of Lok Sabha**__ presides over the joint sitting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

__
 
• The** Deputy Speaker **of the** Lok Sabha presides **over in his **absence**. If **he is also absent,** then the **Deputy Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha presides over it.
 
• The Chairman never presides over the joint sessions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

A** joint sitting **is summoned in the following*** three situations, ***(in which one House passed the Bill and transmitted it to the other House)

 
• If the other House rejects the bill.
 
• disagreements have arisen between the Houses regarding the amendments to be made in the Bill.
 
• If the other House withhold the Bill without being passing it for more than six months.

The** President** is the one who summons the** joint siting.**

 
• **T**he provision for joint sitting is **not **applicable for ***Money bills and Constitution amendment bills.***

questions.question: When the fiscal deficit is high, what happens to the prices?

options.text: There is no direct impact on the prices

questions.solution:

questions.question: UN's Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) elected _________ to the 18-member committee ‘CESCR’ for the Asia Pacific seat in 2018.
questions.solution:
__
 
• UN's Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) elected **Preeti Saran**__ to the 18-member committee ‘CESCR’ for the Asia Pacific seat in 2018.
 
• She was elected for a 4-year term which began on 1 January 2019.
 
• The CESCR was set up by the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) of the UN in 1985.
 
• Its aim is to monitor the implementation of the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (ICESR).
 
• The** President of the United Nations Economic and Social Council** is Mr. **Oh Joon. (As of Oct 2021)**.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure?
questions.solution:
__
 
• A **Sphygmomanometer **__is used to measure blood pressure.
 
• A Thermometer is a device which measures body temperature.
 
• The density of milk is measured by lactometer.
 
• Glucometer monitors or measures blood glucose. It tests the amount of glucose in the blood.

questions.question: In which year was the University Grants Commission (UGC) formally established?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The University Grants Commission (UGC) was formally established in the year **1956**__.
 
• It is a statutory organization which was set up by the Union Government to maintain the standards of university education.
 
• It provides funds for the colleges and universities which are government-recognised.
 
• It is headquartered in New Delhi and has 6 regional centres.

questions.question: When was Indian Super League started?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Indian Super League was founded on 21 October **2013**__.
 
• It was launched with the goal of growing football in India and also to increase its exposure.
 
• It is played in a span of 6 months between 10 teams and organized by All India Football Federation.
 
• Its first season was held in 2014 with 8 teams.

questions.question: Before the 104th Constitutional amendment act 2020, under which article of the Constitution of India can members of the Anglo Indian community be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**331**__.

__
 
• In January 2020, the Anglo-Indian reserved seats in the Parliament and State Legislatures of India were abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 
 
• Om Birla is the 17th and current speaker of Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Under article 331__ of the Constitution of India can members of the Anglo Indian community be nominated to the Lok Sabha by the President.
 
• Article 342 covers The Scheduled Tribes in India.
 
• Article 330 deals with the reservation of seats of SCs and STs in Parliament.
 
• Article 326 was amended in 1988 by the 61st Amendment Act, 1988. It lowered the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• The Rajya Sabha should consist of not more than 250 members - 238 members representing the States and Union Territories, and 12 members nominated by the President. Each member is elected for a term of six years.
 
• Jagdeep Dhankar is the current Chairman of Rajya Sabha and the present Vice-President of India.
 
• **104th Constitutional Amendment Act ceased the reservation of seats for Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative assemblies and extended reservations for SCs and STs for up to ten years. **

questions.question: Which country in the world has the largest number of international borders?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **China and Russia**__ have the largest number of international borders.
 
• Both have 14 neighbouring countries.
 
• The neighbouring countries of China include Mongolia, Russia, Kazakhstan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Bhutan, Nepal, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, Laos, and North Korea.
 
• The neighbouring countries of Russia include Ukraine, Belarus, Latvia, Estonia, Finland, Norway, North Korea, China, Georgia, Mongolia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Lithuania and Poland.

questions.question: Dolly, the first cloned living being created at Roslin Institute in Scotland was a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Sheep__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dolly was a female domestic sheep and the first mammal which was cloned on July 5, 1996__.

 
 
• She was cloned from an adult somatic cell through the process of nuclear transfer.
 
• She was cloned at the Roslin Institute in Midlothian, Scotland, and survived there until her death when she was 6 years old.
 
• Her existence was announced to the public on 22 February 1997.
 
• She was originally code-named “6LL3,” but later on she was named after singer and actress Dolly Parton.
 
 

 
• Cloning

 
 
• Cloning is the production of an exact copy of a cell, any other living part, or a complete organism.
 
• Cloning of an animal was successfully performed for the first time by Ian Wilmut and his colleagues at the Roslin Institute in Edinburgh, Scotland.

questions.question: Mitra Mela was a revolutionary organisation founded by Vinayak Savarkar in the year ________.

questions.question: What is the value of all tangible resources such as raw materials and labour that are used in the production process called?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The value of all tangible resources such as raw materials and labour that are used in the production process is called **real cost**__.
 
• A fixed cost is that which does not change with a decrease or increase in the amount of services or goods sold or produced.
 
• Opportunity Costs are the benefits that an investor or individual misses out when choosing one alternative over other.
 
• Variable Costs are corporate expenses which change in proportion to production output.

questions.question: The term 'Blood Moon' is used to refer to ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The term 'Blood Moon' is used to refer to **Lunar Eclipse**__ since the moon takes on a reddish tinge when it is fully eclipsed.
 
• A lunar eclipse occurs when the moon travels through the umbra of the earth and blocks all direct sunlight.
 
• A solar eclipse occurs when the new moon comes between the earth and the sun, thus blocking the sun rays.

questions.question: The traditional art of 'Jamdani' weaving originated in ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The traditional art of 'Jamdani' weaving originated in Dhaka, **Bangladesh**__.
 
• The Jamdani sarees are also known as Dhakai sarees.
 
• Jam means flower and dani means vase.
 
• Its earliest mention is found in Arthshastra which dates back to 3rd century BC.
 
• The art bloomed the most during the Mughal Period.
